The mutant differs only when `#` is the first character of the identity. Every identity type in ir.ts starts with its kind and a colon, such as `error:` or `cap:`, so `#` is never at index 0.

The mutant differs only when `:effect/` starts at index 0. Every identity type in ir.ts starts with a non-empty kind before its colon, such as `error:effect/SchemaError`, so `:effect/` is never at index 0.

The mutant differs only when the Eq token is the first child of a ConstDecl. parseDeclaration and parseConstBody in parse.ts consume an optional export keyword and the const keyword before the Eq token, so it is never first. A probe parsed 21124 inputs: each fixture whole, at every 11th prefix, and with each line deleted, plus generated const headers. It compared isArrow of every declaration from buildIndex. No input had the Eq token first, and the mutant gave the same output. A control mutant of the value filter differed on 23 inputs.

Name arguments and missing arguments take the same branch under both guards. A non-name expression cannot match an identifier binding. The extra lookup finds no binding or prelude name, then resolves the same expression without changing outerUses.
The text comes from a parsed top-level object, so its first character is `{` or white space. A quoted key never starts at index 0, so `at` is -1 or positive and < and <= agree.

hasDistinctTag is true only for a union root whose members are tagged records with distinct tags, and the early return leaves only a record root or that union root. For a record root hasDistinctTag is false and part is never type inside the union branch, so the term is false in both forms. For the union root, part === type and hasDistinctTag are both true. The root union visits its members with guarded true, so a union below the root has guarded true and the term never changes a result. A differential through guardedRecord over 300,000 forged types matched the source on every row, and 8,297 of the rows were true. A control mutant that drops the term differed.

With && no kind passes the test, so a primitive or a literal reaches the exhaustive check at the end of visit and returns the node itself, a truthy object, in place of true. Each caller of visit reads only the truthiness. The every calls and the union branch coerce the value to a boolean, and the root of guardedRecord is a record or a union, so no root visit returns a primitive or a literal. A differential through guardedRecord over 200,000 forged types matched the source on every row, and 4,296 of the rows were true. A logging copy reached the changed test 30,691 times. A control mutant that passes false for an array element differed.

The guard `colon >= 0` comes first, and `hash` is `id.indexOf("#", colon + 1)`. So `hash` is either -1 or at least colon + 1, and it never equals `colon`. With `colon >= 0`, the tests `hash > colon` and `hash >= colon` give the same truth value. A differential probe through `validateModule` of 22 forged payload ids (empty, colon-only, hash before colon, leading colon, repeated colon and hash) gave identical diagnostics in the source and in the mutated copy.

The early return leaves only a record root or a root union with distinct tags. A union below the root has guarded true, because the root union walks its members with guarded true. A record root has hasDistinctTag false, because hasDistinctTag needs a union root, and part is never type in the union branch for a record root. So the extra term never changes a result. A differential through checkRecursion tested 60,000 random forged modules of three declarations, and every report matched. In 42,863 of them the check reported a cycle. A control mutant that drops the term differed.

The mutant registers a group for a component of one member that has no self edge. That member is a tagged record or an alias, because the test that every member is a tagged record or an alias follows. The reaches walk consults a group only when the source and the target are the same group. For a one-member group that means a self reference, which is a self edge of the graph, so the component is a cycle in the source too. A differential through checkRecursion tested 60,000 random forged modules of three declarations, and every report matched. In those modules the mutant registered a group for an acyclic singleton 264,559 times, and 25,400 of them were tagged records.

A stale change leaves the text and the version unchanged, so the mutant only marks the project dirty. A flush of a started project with no text difference starts no revision, and `#publish` sends a list only when its JSON or the version of its open document changed. A project that has not flushed is already dirty. A differential probe of six stale-change scenarios, at debounce 0 and 50 and with an `effektive/stats` request, matched.

With <=, a frame with no targets left runs one more pass. targets[frame.next] is undefined there, so index[undefined] < 0 and onStack[undefined] are both false, the pass changes nothing, and the next pass pops the frame as before.

With <=, the test also accepts index 0. Only node 0 gets index 0, because the loop visits it first at n = 0 while every index is -1. At every later n, index[n] is -1 or at least 1, so the visits are the same.

The walk never reaches depth 64. Only a member that is a named union alias deepens it: a union nested 70 levels inline emits Option.fromUndefinedOr(u.x). declaration/012 rejects a chain of 64 such aliases (U64 is nested deeper than 128 levels), and a chain of 63 emits the option read. The parser starts each UnaryExpr with its operator token, and a missing operand becomes a Missing node, so neither side of the guard is ever true and || equals &&. The test 'a unary chain deeper than the nesting limit is reported, not checked' in tests/check_unary_test.ts runs 600 nested minus signs and still reaches no undefined operand.

Both exits of checkFit return checker, and each reads it after the call of fits, which records the diagnostic. Negating the test changes no returned value. A differential through the diagnostics of the 86 error fixtures and the examples gave the same output for the source and the mutant. The operand is never undefined (see BodyChecker.unary). With && the guard also lets a ! node through, but the operand of ! is boolean, and linear gives undefined for a boolean literal, path, comparison, or connective, so the result is undefined either way.

The guard runs when a Name node of a NamePattern has no text. The parser builds a NamePattern only from an identifier token, so the name always has text. With false, declareLocal also returns early for a name without text, so no binding or diagnostic differs.

The guard only decides whether to call expr on the last child of a top-level const. For an undefined node or a type kind, expr takes its default branch and does nothing, because kindOf gives undefined for an undefined node and no type kind is an expression kind. With || the extra calls reach only those nodes. The probe analyzed 19169 inputs: each fixtures file whole, at every 11th prefix, and with each line deleted. A copy that logs each time the two forms differ saw 2046 such cases. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy in all of them.

With >=, an empty CallExpr calls expr on an undefined node, and expr does nothing for it: kindOf gives undefined and the switch takes its default branch. The parser wraps the callee to make a CallExpr, so the node always has a child, and the log copy saw no empty CallExpr in 19169 inputs. A forced probe emptied kids in two copies, with > and with >=. The outputs matched on all 19169 inputs, so the empty case has no effect.

With >=, an empty PipeExpr calls expr on an undefined node, and expr does nothing for it: kindOf gives undefined and the switch takes its default branch. The parser wraps the left operand to make a PipeExpr, so the node always has a child, and the log copy saw no empty PipeExpr in 19169 inputs. A forced probe emptied kids in two copies, with > and with >=. The outputs matched on all 19169 inputs, so the empty case has no effect.

With >=, a MatchExpr without children calls expr on an undefined node, and expr does nothing for it: kindOf gives undefined and the switch takes its default branch. Error recovery can build such a node. The probe analyzed 19169 inputs: each fixtures file whole, at every 11th prefix, and with each line deleted. A copy that logs each time the two forms differ saw 23 empty MatchExpr nodes. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy in all of them.

With ||, a shorthand field {a} gets fieldLabel on its name. The next statement, declareLocal on the same name node, sets a local target for it and replaces the field target. Every path of declareLocal that has a name sets that target, and a block always has a scope. A BindingField always has a first name, because the parser calls parseName before it. The probe analyzed 19169 inputs: each fixtures file whole, at every 11th prefix, and with each line deleted. A copy that logs each time the two forms differ saw 2319 shorthand fields. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy in all of them.

A CtorPattern always has a first Name. The parser builds it at one site, and it calls parseName for the constructor before it builds the node. So names is never empty and the >= form never runs on an empty list. The log copy saw no empty list in 19169 inputs. No forced probe applies: ctorRef on an undefined node reads an unrelated node, so the empty case is unreachable, not harmless.

The sort runs on occurrences whose span text passes isIdentifier, so each span is one run of identifier characters. Two different occurrences cannot overlap or touch, and they never share a start with different ends. The && form returns the end difference for spans with different starts and 0 for spans with the same start. That has the sign of the source result when the spans are disjoint, and spans with the same start and the same end give 0 in both forms. So the forms differ only for spans that share a start with different ends, or that overlap. The probe analyzed 7844 inputs and 704897 occurrences. It found 0 touching pairs, 0 overlapping pairs that are not identical, and 0 pairs with the same start and different ends. A copy that logs the comparator saw 1553777 calls and 0 whose sign differed from the || form. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy for every input. The case cannot be forced, because the spans of two occurrences cannot share a start with different ends.

The <= form differs from the < form only when an occurrence A ends at the offset and another occurrence B comes first in the list and holds the offset inside its span. The source reaches A with its second find. So A and B would overlap or touch. Occurrence spans are runs of identifier characters, so they never do. The probe analyzed 7844 inputs and 704897 occurrences. It found 0 touching pairs and 0 overlapping pairs that are not identical. A copy that logs the case saw 2114691 evaluations where the two forms of the test disagree, at the end of a name. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy for every input, at the edges of each name and at every 13th offset. As a check of the probe, a copy that changed the test of the start of the span changed 7554 output lines.

In the second find the end of the span equals the offset, and an end is never below its start. So start <= offset always holds, and the <= form differs from the < form only for a span with start equal to end. The symbol index keeps only the occurrences whose text passes isIdentifier, and that function rejects the empty text. So no occurrence has an empty span. The probe found 0 empty spans in 704897 occurrences. A copy that logs the case saw 0 evaluations where the two forms disagree, in 1688773650 evaluations. The output of the mutant copy matched the source copy for every input. The case cannot be forced, because an empty span never enters the index.

The mutant returns true from the walk visitor for a Token node. The walk then reads the children of that node. A Token node has no children, because the parser makes each token a leaf, so the walk visits nothing more and the printed text does not change. A scan of 190 fixture files found 45450 Token nodes with 0 children. A differential through printTree over 3990 texts, which are each fixture file cut at three lengths with seven tails, gave the same output for the source and the mutant.

The comparison guards the read of the next token kind for the keyword check of an identifier. The lexer always ends the token list with an Eof token, so the last token never has kind Ident, and the guard is never evaluated at the last token. With <=, the guard would differ only there. A copy that logs the case counted 2,077,973 evaluations in 12214 inputs (each fixture whole, with each third line deleted, and at every 17th prefix) and 0 evaluations at the last token. The mutant copy gave output identical to the source on all 12214 inputs.
